assertions.text: List values in the table use bracket syntax like [tech:java, biz:sales, dev:ci] — not comma-separated strings without brackets.
Empty list input uses [] (not a blank cell, which represents null). The distinction between empty list and null is preserved.
assertions.evidence: empty list returns empty list | [] ... and null category returns all tags | ... | (blank cell) | ...

assertions.text: Values containing pipes (|) or brackets are properly quoted or escaped so they don't conflict with table syntax.
assertions.evidence: pipe in biz tag preserved for business | ["biz:hr|recruiting", tech:go] | business | ["biz:hr|recruiting"] and brackets in tech tag preserved | ["tech:[ci]", biz:sales] | tech | ["tech:[ci]"]

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Tags | Category | Filtered? (Scenario is leftmost column)

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Filtered tags?' or 'Result?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Tag filtering by category") and void shouldFilterTagsByCategory(...)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence:
@Description("""
        Open: behaviour for unknown category values (not "tech" or "business")
        is unspecified. Prefix matching is assumed to be case-sensitive.
        """)
